result.summary: The environment is highly car-oriented, characterized by a multi-lane roadway with no visible pedestrian infrastructure such as sidewalks or marked crossings. A metal guardrail on the left side of the road physically separates the paved surface from a wooded area, leaving no safe space for pedestrians to walk or seek refuge from traffic.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Facilities
hazards.description: There are no sidewalks or designated walking paths, forcing any pedestrians to walk directly in the roadway or on a narrow, unprotected shoulder.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the roadway throughout the visible frame

hazards.name: Physical Entrapment by Guardrail
hazards.description: The metal guardrail prevents pedestrians from stepping off the roadway into the grass/wooded area to avoid oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the roadway

hazards.name: High-Speed Roadway Geometry
hazards.description: Wide lanes and long, clear sightlines encourage high vehicle speeds in an area without pedestrian protection.
hazards.location_in_image: Main travel lanes

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a paved sidewalk behind the guardrail or by reclaiming road space to provide a dedicated, separated path for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Road Diet / Lane Narrowing
interventions.description: Reduce the number or width of travel lanes to slow vehicle speeds and create space for a protected bike lane or wider pedestrian buffer.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Crossing Improvements
interventions.description: If there is a need for crossing, install high-visibility marked crosswalks and potentially a pedestrian refuge island given the road width.

result.summary: This residential intersection provides basic sidewalk infrastructure but lacks any marked crosswalks or pedestrian-oriented traffic controls. The wide, unmarked roadway and parked vehicles near the corner create potential visibility issues and may encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crosswalk
hazards.description: The intersection lacks painted markings to designate a safe crossing area, reducing driver awareness of pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground at the intersection of the two streets.

hazards.name: Wide Unmarked Roadway
hazards.description: The lack of lane markings on a wide road can encourage higher vehicle speeds and unpredictable lane positioning.
hazards.location_in_image: Main roadway in the foreground.

hazards.name: Parked Vehicle Obstruction
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection corner can block the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the side street, near the corner.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental or ladder-style crosswalk markings to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the roadway at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the intersection to improve sightlines for all road users.

result.summary: The image shows a well-maintained sidewalk separated from a multi-lane roadway by a grass verge and mature trees. However, there is a complete lack of pedestrian crossing infrastructure at this junction, including marked crosswalks, curb ramps, or signals.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossing
hazards.description: There are no painted crosswalks at the intersection, requiring pedestrians to cross unmarked lanes of traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground roadway intersection

hazards.name: Missing curb ramps
hazards.description: The sidewalk ends at a vertical curb without a ramp, creating an accessibility barrier for mobility-impaired users.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the sidewalk in the foreground

hazards.name: Sight line obstruction
hazards.description: Dense vegetation and the curve of the road may limit the visibility of pedestrians to oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the roadway curve

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install directional curb ramps with detectable warning surfaces to ensure accessibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Warning Signage
interventions.description: Install signage to alert drivers of the potential presence of pedestrians at the crossing point.

result.summary: The image depicts a two-lane roadway completely lacking pedestrian infrastructure, with no sidewalks, crosswalks, or lighting. A guardrail on the right side creates a physical barrier that would trap a pedestrian on the roadway edge in the event of oncoming traffic.

hazards.name: Absence of Sidewalks
hazards.description: Pedestrians have no dedicated space and must share the high-speed roadway with vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the road, adjacent to the guardrail.

hazards.name: Guardrail Entrapment
hazards.description: The guardrail prevents pedestrians from stepping off the road into the green space to avoid vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the road.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Construction
interventions.description: Add a separated sidewalk or multi-use path behind the guardrail or by relocating it.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing and Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Reduce lane widths to encourage lower speeds and provide space for a shoulder or bike lane.
